instructions: Fill a wide pot about halfway with water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Use less water than you would for other pasta. The sauce needs the water to be starchy.
Meanwhile, finely grate all 8 oz of the pecorino on the small holes of a box grater. Put about 1 cup of it aside for the table and the rest in a medium bowl.
Coarsely grind the 1 tbsp peppercorns in a pepper mill, or crush them in a mortar. Put about a third of the pepper aside with the table cheese.
When the water boils, add the 2 tsp salt and the 1 lb spaghetti. Cook it for half the time the package says, stirring now and then. It finishes cooking in the skillet.
While it cooks, heat a large skillet over medium and add the rest of the pepper to the dry pan. Stir it for about 1 minute, until it smells strong and toasty. Don't let it smoke.
Ladle about 1 cup of the pasta water into the skillet. It'll hiss and bubble.

Lift the spaghetti into the skillet with tongs, and keep the pot of water on the stove. Toss and shake the pan over medium for 4 to 5 minutes, adding a splash of pasta water whenever it looks dry, until the spaghetti is just tender with a little bite. You want a few spoonfuls of cloudy liquid left in the pan.
While the spaghetti finishes, stir a few tablespoons of hot pasta water into the cheese in the bowl with a fork, a little at a time, until it's a thick, smooth paste with no dry bits.

Take the skillet off the heat and wait 30 seconds. Add the cheese paste and toss quickly with the tongs until a creamy sauce coats every strand. If it looks thick or clumpy, add a splash more pasta water and keep tossing. Keep the pan off the heat. Too hot and the cheese turns stringy.
Taste a strand. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve right away, with the pecorino and pepper you kept for the table.
method_notes: All three versions are only spaghetti, Pecorino Romano and black pepper bound with starchy pasta water, with no butter. Pina Bresciani cooks the pasta half its time in a shallow pot of lightly salted water, finishes it in the pan with toasted pepper and pasta water, then stirs in a pecorino paste off the heat after 30 seconds. Vincenzo's Plate also makes a cheese paste and melts it over steam from the pasta pot, while America's Test Kitchen whisks the cheese with pasta water, a little cream and oil and tosses everything in a bowl. This one follows Pina's method and ratios, doubled for four.
